records.record_text: The transitional President expressed his Government’s commitment to the return of constitutional rule in the country, noting that gaining the confidence of the Malian people and promoting reconciliation would be the priority achieved by improving security and initiating key reforms.
records.actor_source: Colonel Assimi Goïta, Transitional President of Mali
records.political_signal: Malian transitional government publicly commits to constitutional rule while highlighting required national dialogue reforms.
records.policy_implication: Framing national dialogue as a prerequisite may create friction with international electoral deadlines.

records.record_text: Members of the Security Council reiterated their call for the Malian transitional authorities to achieve the political transition and the return to constitutional order within the agreed timeline set out in the transition charter and in accordance with the commitments of the transitional authorities and the decisions of ECOWAS.
records.political_signal: Firm Security Council endorsement of ECOWAS timelines for Mali's transition.
records.policy_implication: Maintains international pressure on Malian authorities to publish an electoral calendar and hold elections by 27 February 2022.

records.record_text: During the Council's visit to the region, the transitional Government of Mali declared the Special Representative of ECOWAS in Mali persona non grata and gave him 72 hours to leave the country.
records.political_signal: Escalation of diplomatic tension between Malian transitional authorities and regional body ECOWAS.
records.policy_implication: Complicates regional mediation and international oversight of the political transition.

records.record_text: The Security Council welcomed the renewed commitment of the transitional authorities to expediting the implementation of the Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation in Mali, including the transitional Government's recent proposal to integrate 13,000 former rebel combatants into the army in the coming months.
records.political_signal: Positive signal acknowledging concrete government proposals regarding disarmament and integration.
records.policy_implication: Requires follow-through by signatory movements to finalize accelerated DDR.

records.record_text: The Coordination des mouvements de l'Azawad and the Platform coalitions of armed groups deplored that, six years after the signing of the Agreement, peace dividends were sparse and the development component had registered very little progress, attributing this to a perceived lack of political will by Malian authorities.
records.political_signal: Signatory armed groups express deep frustration with central authority implementation of the Algiers Agreement.
records.policy_implication: Risk of peace process stagnation or renewed insecurity in northern Mali if development and decentralization components are not fulfilled.

records.record_text: Leadership of MINUSMA highlighted the continued degradation of the security situation in Mali, with 500 incidents since the start of 2021, and noted that local communities in many zones had no choice but to sign local agreements imposed by armed groups dictating rigorous conditions.
records.political_signal: Highlighting severe erosion of state presence and expansion of violent extremist governance.
records.policy_implication: Underscores need for enhanced civilian protection and state redeployment.

records.record_text: The Special Representative for Mali saw the proposed increase in the uniformed personnel ceiling recommended by the Secretary-General in report S/2021/657 as an absolute necessity owing to the dangers faced in the north and the lack of personnel in the centre.
records.actor_source: El Ghassim Wane, SRSG for Mali
records.political_signal: Direct plea from UN leadership on the ground for additional troop capacity.
records.policy_implication: Requires decision by the Security Council on increasing MINUSMA authorized troop ceiling.

records.record_text: MINUSMA deplored the new strategy of village encirclement used by terrorist groups, which was expected to significantly increase the number of Malians needing humanitarian assistance, while vital infrastructure was increasingly targeted and only 31.5 per cent of the humanitarian response plan had been financed.
records.political_signal: Alarm call on extremist tactics exacerbating humanitarian crises amid severe donor funding shortages.
records.policy_implication: Urgent requirement for humanitarian resource mobilization and counter-encirclement protection strategies.

records.record_text: UNICEF and UN country team members highlighted that 1,664 schools were closed in Mali due to insecurity, affecting 500,000 children, while the combined pandemic and sociopolitical crisis pushed an additional 900,000 people into poverty.
records.political_signal: Demonstrates deep socio-economic and developmental reversal in Mali.
records.policy_implication: Demands targeted education, youth protection, and economic mitigation programming.

records.record_text: The Security Council urged the Malian transitional authorities and signatory armed groups to make further progress to effectively fulfil the priority measures referred to in paragraph 4 of Council resolution 2584 (2021) before the end of the current MINUSMA mandate.
records.political_signal: Clear Council mandate benchmark set for evaluating Malian implementation progress.
records.policy_implication: Future MINUSMA mandate renewal will evaluate compliance with resolution 2584 (2021).

records.record_text: The President of the Niger stressed that the country retained control of its territory but remained the target of external threats originating mainly from neighbouring countries, expressing serious concerns over the deteriorating security situation in Mali affecting regional stability.
records.actor_source: Mohamed Bazoum, President of the Niger
records.political_signal: Niger highlights cross-border spillover risks while asserting domestic territorial control.
records.policy_implication: Regional stabilization depends directly on containing cross-border militant movements from Mali.

records.record_text: The Minister for Foreign Affairs of the Niger stated that defence and security spending had increased from 5 per cent of the State budget in 2010 to almost 20 per cent in 2020, and requested the Security Council to find a mechanism to provide lasting and predictable funding for counter-terrorism efforts.
records.actor_source: Hassoumi Massoudou, Foreign Minister of the Niger
records.political_signal: High fiscal burden of defense on developing frontline states necessitates UN multilateral funding.
records.policy_implication: Reopens Council debate on UN assessed contributions for regional counter-terrorism operations.

records.record_text: President Bazoum and Foreign Minister Massoudou expressed concern over the defiance of the Malian transitional authorities towards regional partners, questioned the rationale for prioritizing national dialogue over elections, and condemned the expulsion of the ECOWAS Special Representative.
records.political_signal: Strong criticism from democratic neighbour Niger against Malian transition delays and anti-ECOWAS stances.
records.policy_implication: Reflects regional solidarity within ECOWAS/G5 against unconstitutional changes of government.

records.record_text: The Commander of the G5 Sahel Joint Force outlined key operational challenges including command coordination, air capabilities, surveillance, and logistical autonomy, advocating for a campaign plan focused on Force operationalization and partner cooperation.
records.actor_source: Major General Oumar Bikimo, Commander of G5 Sahel Joint Force
records.political_signal: Joint Force requires structural support and capacity enhancement to execute its military campaign effectively.
records.policy_implication: Highlighting logistical gaps supports requests for a dedicated support mechanism.

records.record_text: While the Minister for Foreign Affairs of the Niger and the G5 Sahel Commander advocated the creation of a dedicated UN support office for the Force, Security Council members expressed differing views, with some reiterating reservations about UN funding for counter-terrorism operations.
records.actor_source: Government of the Niger / G5 Sahel Commander
records.political_signal: Continued division within the Security Council regarding UN assessed funding for enforcement operations.
records.policy_implication: Alternative bilateral and multilateral financing models must be explored in lieu of UN assessed funding consensus.

records.record_text: President Bazoum highlighted education as his top priority to tackle poverty, demographic growth, and early marriage, noting that the Niger suffered from historical structural adjustment programmes that drastically reduced public education personnel.
records.actor_source: Mohamed Bazoum, President of the Niger
records.political_signal: Linking educational investment directly to long-term conflict prevention and counter-radicalization.
records.policy_implication: Calls for international financial institutions and UN agencies to prioritize social infrastructure investment.

records.record_text: The UN Country Team in the Niger informed the Council that only 30 per cent of the humanitarian response was funded, leaving two-thirds of beneficiaries unassisted, while climate change fallout was exacerbating land degradation, displacement, and food insecurity.
records.actor_source: UN Country Team in the Niger
records.political_signal: Severe human security vulnerabilities threatened by climate degradation and donor shortfalls.
records.policy_implication: Risk to SDG achievement during the decade of action unless emergency funding and resilience building are scaled up.

records.record_text: Security Council members commended the Niger for its democratic accomplishments, making the country a role model for the region, and recognized its remarkable contributions to the Council, ECOWAS, and the G5 Sahel.
records.political_signal: Strong Council validation of the Niger's constitutional democracy and constructive multilateral role.
records.policy_implication: Reinforces diplomatic backing for the Niger as a regional anchor state.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to the Republic of Colombia

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Peace Agreement Verification and Political Engagement Mission
main_risks: Persistently high numbers of killings of social leaders, human rights defenders, and former FARC-EP combatants
Security vacuums in former conflict zones exploited by illegal armed groups and illicit economies
Political polarization and potential budget cuts threatening transitional justice institutions
main_commitments: Joint request by the Government of Colombia and FARC to extend the UN Verification Mission mandate for one year
Reaffirmation by FARC party leadership of its irreversible commitment to the peace process
Government commitment to continue funding and supporting ex-combatant reintegration and peace implementation
main_policy_signals: Unanimous UN Security Council support for the comprehensive and integrated implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement
Critical need to establish a comprehensive non-militarized State presence in former conflict areas
Imperative of preserving the independence, autonomy, and funding of transitional justice bodies
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Colombia (11–14 July 2019) reaffirmed unanimous international support for the 2016 Final Peace Agreement. Engaging with President Iván Duque, senior cabinet officials, congressional peace commissions across political spectrums, FARC party leadership, civil society, transitional justice leaders, the UN Country Team, and local indigenous communities in Cauca Department, the Council reviewed progress in ex-combatant reintegration and transitional justice. The mission identified the ongoing wave of killings of social leaders and former combatants, security vacuums, and deep political polarization as primary threats to peace consolidation.

records.record_text: President Duque affirmed his commitment to the peace process, emphasizing that implementation progress during his administration exceeded prior achievements, including approving 24 productive projects for ex-combatants and updating the land register.
records.political_signal: Demonstrating national ownership and commitment to the Final Peace Agreement.
records.policy_implication: Reassuring international partners regarding the government's stabilization agenda.

records.record_text: President Duque submitted a formal request to the Security Council on behalf of the Government and FARC to renew the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for another year starting 26 September 2019.
records.political_signal: Bipartite consensus on the essential role of international verification.
records.policy_implication: Provides mandate authorization basis for extending the UN Verification Mission.

records.record_text: President Duque acknowledged grave concern over killings of community leaders, human rights defenders, and ex-FARC members, highlighting protection schemes and national action plans concentrated in 50 drug trafficking and illegal mining municipalities.
records.political_signal: Recognition of ongoing security vulnerabilities in former conflict zones.
records.policy_implication: Requires targeting protective measures and law enforcement resources in high-risk areas.

records.record_text: Security Council members emphasized unanimous support for the implementation of the Final Agreement as an integrated package, welcoming the mandate extension request while expressing strong concern over killings of social leaders and former combatants.
records.political_signal: Unanimous international backing for peace agreement integrity and violence cessation.
records.policy_implication: Sustaining international oversight and demanding enhanced security guarantees.

records.record_text: Opposition and independent legislators commended FARC political participation but criticized selective implementation by the government, noting delays in rural reform, legal insecurity, and security failures in former conflict areas.
records.political_signal: Highlighting domestic political polarization and implementation gaps.
records.policy_implication: Calls for cross-party dialogue to build legislative consensus around peace implementation.

records.record_text: Governing party legislators argued that plebiscite objections remained unaddressed, criticizing the transitional justice system for favoring perpetrators over victims and asserting peace accords expanded illicit coca crops.
records.political_signal: Persistent political resistance to original peace agreement provisions.
records.policy_implication: Risk of ongoing legal challenges and polarization surrounding transitional justice.

records.record_text: FARC party leadership reaffirmed its irreversible commitment to the peace process and institutional framework, explicitly distancing itself from dissident leaders who abandoned the accord while urging faster project approvals and legal guarantees.
records.political_signal: Mainstream ex-guerrilla commitment to peaceful democratic engagement.
records.policy_implication: Needs robust state support for economic reintegration to retain ex-combatants in licit life.

records.record_text: Civil society representatives reported that non-militarized state presence remains absent in many regions, resulting in fear, forced displacement, child recruitment, and systematic violence against ethnic and community leaders.
records.political_signal: Urgent civil society call to address rural protection vacuums.
records.policy_implication: Requires comprehensive non-militarized state institutional expansion.

records.record_text: Leaders of transitional justice institutions expressed grave concern that proposed government budget cuts could severely impede the operations of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace, Truth Commission, and Search Unit.
records.actor_target: Government of Colombia / UN Security Council
records.political_signal: Institutional vulnerability of transitional justice bodies.
records.policy_implication: Demands budget protection and international political support for transitional justice.

records.record_text: The Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP) reported that over 11,000 FARC members, 2,000 public security force members, and 53 civilians voluntarily submitted to its jurisdiction, with 7 major cases open involving 830,000 victims.
records.political_signal: Tangible procedural progress in transitional justice delivery.
records.policy_implication: Demonstrates functioning judicial mechanisms requiring sustained operational autonomy.

records.record_text: Community leaders in Cauca Department attributed intense regional violence to competing illegal armed groups, illegal mining and drug trade, and targeted attacks against defenders of land and voluntary crop substitution.
records.political_signal: Highlighting structural conflict drivers in high-risk departments.
records.policy_implication: Necessitates targeted rural development, voluntary substitution support, and Indigenous Guard empowerment.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission observed successful ex-combatant productive initiatives at Santa Rosa ETCR, including an agricultural tree tomato project employing ex-combatants and local community members, while noting persistent security threats.
records.political_signal: Validation of ground-level community-integrated ex-combatant economic activity.
records.policy_implication: Encouraging continued financial and technical support for joint community-ex-combatant projects.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Côte d’Ivoire and Guinea-Bissau

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Peace Transition Review and Electoral Crisis Prevention
main_risks: Recurring political instability and institutional paralysis in Guinea-Bissau stemming from constitutional ambiguities and deep political mistrust
Irregularities and voter list discrepancies in the biometric voter registration process in Guinea-Bissau threatening electoral credibility
Social unrest, teacher strikes, and violent student protests potentially disrupting the electoral process in Guinea-Bissau
Persistent root causes of conflict in Côte d'Ivoire and Liberia including land disputes, national reconciliation deficits, and weak decentralization
Transnational organized crime, drug trafficking, and corruption exploiting institutional weakness in Guinea-Bissau
main_commitments: Signing of the Stability Pact and Code of Conduct by competing political parties in Guinea-Bissau
Security Council commitment to supporting political dialogue, democratic consolidation, and full implementation of the Conakry Agreement
Ivorian Government commitment to hosting inclusive dialogue on electoral reform and funding reconciliation and DDR processes
International donor commitment to supporting election basket funds and transition peacebuilding programmes
main_policy_signals: Imperative of holding free, fair, transparent legislative elections in Guinea-Bissau on 10 March 2019 and presidential elections in 2019
Critical need for post-election constitutional reform in Guinea-Bissau to establish clear division of executive, legislative, and judicial powers
Emphasis on careful transition planning, capacity mapping, and long-term peacebuilding funding when drawing down UN peacekeeping operations
Call for inclusive political governance, national dialogue, and credible elections in Côte d'Ivoire in 2020 to consolidate peace gains
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Côte d’Ivoire and Guinea-Bissau (14–16 February 2019) reviewed peace transition processes in Côte d'Ivoire and Liberia and engaged key national and international actors in Guinea-Bissau ahead of its critical legislative elections. In Abidjan, the Council evaluated lessons learned from UNOCI's closure, emphasizing the need to sustain national reconciliation, DDR, SSR, and social cohesion prior to the 2020 Ivorian presidential elections. In Bissau, the mission focused on breaking the cycle of constitutional crises by demanding adherence to the Conakry Agreement, supporting the 14 February 2019 Stability Pact, addressing biometric voter registration anomalies, urging timely elections on 10 March 2019, and preparing for a phased reconfiguration of UNIOGBIS.

records.record_text: Vice-President Duncan expressed appreciation for the work of UNOCI and suggested that the case of Côte d'Ivoire be used as a model for countries making the transition from peacekeeping to peacebuilding.
records.political_signal: Promoting Côte d'Ivoire's peace transition as a benchmark model for UN peacekeeping exits.
records.policy_implication: UN transition frameworks should incorporate lessons from Côte d'Ivoire regarding national ownership and regional cooperation.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission co-lead renewed strong commitment to the sovereignty and integrity of Côte d'Ivoire, highlighting the need to strengthen national reconciliation, dialogue, DDR, and SSR to prevent conflict reoccurrence.
records.political_signal: Reaffirming UN support while emphasizing mandatory sustained national reforms post-UNOCI.
records.policy_implication: Sustained peace requires continuous national investments in DDR, SSR, and inclusive governance.

records.record_text: The Vice-President informed the mission that 93 per cent of former combatants had been reintegrated, and the Foreign Minister noted the Government financed 72 per cent of the DDR programme over a three-year period.
records.political_signal: Demonstrating high national financial ownership and concrete achievements in post-conflict reintegration.
records.policy_implication: High domestic budgetary contribution is critical for effective and sustainable DDR execution.

records.record_text: The UN Resident Coordinator for Côte d'Ivoire identified land conflicts and issues related to the management of natural resources as remaining root causes of conflict in Côte d'Ivoire.
records.actor_source: UN Resident Coordinator for Côte d'Ivoire
records.political_signal: Warning that economic growth alone does not eliminate underlying structural drivers of conflict.
records.policy_implication: Post-mission peacebuilding programmes must prioritize land reform and resource governance.

records.record_text: The UN Resident Coordinator for Liberia identified three main drivers of conflict in Liberia: land issues, respect for human rights, and accountability for crimes committed during the civil war, calling on the Security Council to look at Liberia through a lens of prevention.
records.political_signal: Cautioning against premature international disengagement following peacekeeping mission exit.
records.policy_implication: The Council should maintain active political oversight and peacebuilding funding after mission drawdown.

records.record_text: The Security Council delegation called upon Ivorian authorities to continue to consolidate democracy through free, fair, credible and peaceful elections in 2020 and enhance national reconciliation.
records.political_signal: Highlighting the 2020 elections as a vital test for long-term democratic stability in Côte d'Ivoire.
records.policy_implication: Electoral support and inclusive political dialogue must remain central to UN Country Team priorities.

records.record_text: Prime Minister Aristides Gomes noted that competing political parties in Guinea-Bissau signed the Stability Pact on 14 February 2019, obliging signatories to accept election results and implement institutional reforms.
records.political_signal: Welcoming a key consensual framework designed to ensure post-election political stability.
records.policy_implication: International actors must hold political signatories accountable to the terms of the Stability Pact.

records.record_text: Prime Minister Gomes noted technical problems with voter registration and voter list discrepancies in Guinea-Bissau, informing that ECOWAS experts were auditing the electoral lists to ensure credibility.
records.political_signal: Acknowledging voter registration deficiencies while reassuring partners through regional technical audit.
records.policy_implication: Immediate technical and audit support is required to prevent contested election outcomes.

records.record_text: Prime Minister Gomes reported political actors manipulating social unrest, agitating student protests, and infiltrating demonstrations to trigger violence and obstruct the legislative elections.
records.political_signal: Exposing political spoiling tactics aimed at destabilizing the agreed electoral timetable.
records.policy_implication: Enhanced electoral security arrangements and prompt appointment of an Interior Minister are critical.

records.record_text: Prime Minister Gomes argued that any plan to reconfigure UNIOGBIS should be discussed with the Government and support national efforts to undertake key institutional reforms.
records.political_signal: Insisting on national consultation and alignment before UN mission drawdown or mandate changes.
records.policy_implication: UNIOGBIS transition planning must be closely coordinated with state authorities.

records.record_text: Prime Minister Gomes highlighted weak State institutions and infiltration making efforts to combat drug trafficking and organized crime challenging, requiring political will and external assistance.
records.political_signal: Conceding state vulnerability to transnational organized crime and corruption.
records.policy_implication: Post-election support must focus heavily on anti-narcotics, maritime security, and justice sector capacity.

records.record_text: The Group of Five highlighted that recurring political crises in Guinea-Bissau were caused by deep mistrust among national actors, institutional fragility, rampant corruption, and divergent constitutional interpretations.
records.political_signal: Consensus among international partners that systemic structural reforms are indispensable for lasting stability.
records.policy_implication: Elections alone will not resolve the crisis without subsequent constitutional and anti-corruption reforms.

records.record_text: The Speaker of Parliament noted that voter registration problems were exacerbated when the Prosecutor General suspended Technical Support Office activities and expelled Nigerian technical experts.
records.political_signal: Illustrating how institutional overreach and judicial interference disrupted electoral preparation.
records.policy_implication: Strengthening institutional coordination and legal clarity is vital during electoral cycles.

records.record_text: Representatives of non-parliamentary political parties denounced irregularities in voter registration, requested publication of the ECOWAS audit report, and called for Security Council support for inclusive elections.
records.political_signal: Expressing political mistrust and demanding full transparency on voter rolls to prevent boycott or rejection of results.
records.policy_implication: Electoral authorities must ensure total transparency in voter roll corrections to preserve inclusivity.

records.record_text: Civil society representatives urged the United Nations not to abandon Guinea-Bissau, requesting support for peaceful elections, post-election government stability, and security, public service, and justice reforms.
records.political_signal: High public expectation for continued UN engagement to guarantee political stability and reform.
records.policy_implication: The Council must carefully calibrate UNIOGBIS reconfiguration to avoid creating a peacebuilding vacuum.

records.record_text: President José Mário Vaz reassured the mission that all conditions were in place for holding legislative elections on 10 March, emphasizing that military forces remained calm because he respected their chain of command.
records.political_signal: Claiming credit for keeping the military out of politics and committing to holding legislative elections.
records.policy_implication: Military non-interference must be sustained throughout the legislative and presidential election cycles.

records.record_text: President Vaz appealed to the Security Council for the lifting of UN sanctions against military officers in Guinea-Bissau, stating that former freedom fighters needed support and compensation to leave barracks.
records.political_signal: Advocating on behalf of sanctioned military officers and linking SSR/pensions to military stability.
records.policy_implication: Sanctions review should be linked to verifiable political neutrality, SSR progress, and compliance with constitutional order.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission strongly advocated political dialogue for full implementation of the Conakry Agreement, holding legislative elections on 10 March and presidential elections in 2019, and pursuing constitutional reform.
records.political_signal: Firm international mandate demanding strict compliance with electoral timelines and Conakry Agreement commitments.
records.policy_implication: Council monitoring and possible targeted measures remain tools to enforce compliance with electoral schedules.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission urged bodies concerned in Guinea-Bissau to rectify voter registration irregularities to enable disenfranchised citizens to vote, and encouraged adherence to the Stability Pact and Code of Conduct.
records.political_signal: Direct call to fix electoral grievances transparently to prevent post-election contesting of results.
records.policy_implication: Electoral assistance units and ECOWAS must provide urgent technical support for voter roll reconciliation.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 5–7 October 2018

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Electoral process and political transition engagement
main_risks: Lack of political consensus on key electoral modalities including voting machines and the voter registry
Persistent insecurity and armed group activity in eastern DRC, particularly Beni, Ituri, Tanganyika, and Kasai
Restrictions on political space, peaceful assembly, and freedom of expression
Ebola virus disease outbreak compounding insecurity and electoral organization challenges
Potential post-electoral instability driven by widespread mistrust among opposition and civil society
main_commitments: DRC Government commitment to holding and funding elections on 23 December 2018
Opposition commitment to participate in elections without boycott and unify around a single candidate
CENCO commitment to deploy 40,000 electoral observers
MONUSCO commitment to remain available for technical, logistical, and civilian protection support
main_policy_signals: Reaffirmation of full respect for DRC sovereignty and independence in managing internal affairs
Emphasis on the necessity of inclusive, free, fair, credible, and peaceful elections for long-term national stability
Call for full implementation of confidence-building measures under the 31 December 2016 political agreement
Reiteration of MONUSCO's crucial role in protecting civilians and supporting the electoral process if requested
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to the Democratic Republic of the Congo (5–7 October 2018) aimed to support the country's upcoming 23 December elections, intended to mark its first peaceful transfer of power. While the DRC Government emphasized its national sovereignty and financial independence in organizing the polls, the Council identified significant political polarization and mistrust regarding electoral mechanics—specifically the use of voting machines and voter registry integrity. Opposition parties and civil society expressed deep concern over restricted political space, candidate exclusions, and security threats in the east, whereas religious leaders and UN entities underscored the urgent need for consensus-building, protection of civilians, and sustained technical support.

activities.activity_description: Meeting with the Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI)
Meeting with the President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Joseph Kabila Kabange
Meeting with the Prime Minister, Vice-Prime Minister/Minister of Interior and Security, and national security officials
Meeting with representatives of the presidential majority (Front commun pour le Congo)
Meeting with political opposition delegation members
Meeting with female presidential and legislative candidates
Meeting with the Conférence épiscopale nationale du Congo (CENCO)
Meeting with civil society organizations, youth movement activists, and human rights groups
Briefing by MONUSCO senior leadership and the United Nations country team
Concluding press conference co-chaired by mission leads

actors_met.actor_name: Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI)
Joseph Kabila Kabange, President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
Prime Minister and Vice-Prime Minister / Minister of Interior and Security
National Intelligence Agency (ANR) and Military Intelligence Service
Front commun pour le Congo (FCC - Presidential Majority)
Opposition Delegation (UNC, UDPS, Dynamique de l'opposition, Nouvel Élan, Ensemble pour le changement, MLC, Synergie électorale notre Congo)
Female Candidates for Presidential and Legislative Elections
Conférence épiscopale nationale du Congo (CENCO)
Civil Society Organizations (Women rights, youth activists, human rights, and eastern DRC groups)
MONUSCO Senior Leadership
United Nations Country Team (UNCT)

records.record_text: The President of the Independent National Electoral Commission confirmed that both the electoral calendar and the legal framework were in place for holding the presidential, national and provincial legislative elections on 23 December, as scheduled.
records.political_signal: Demonstrates technical readiness and official schedule adherence for the DRC elections.
records.policy_implication: Reaffirms the deadline for national elections without postponement.

records.record_text: Council members welcomed progress made to date and noted the decision of the Government to take full responsibility for organizing and funding the elections, while stressing that the aim of their visit was to support the electoral process in full respect for the sovereignty of the country.
records.actor_target: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
records.political_signal: Signals support for DRC's electoral process while respecting national sovereignty and financial self-reliance.
records.policy_implication: Frames international engagement as advisory and respectful of DRC sovereign decisions.

records.record_text: Referring to the mandate of MONUSCO, Council members reiterated the Mission's availability to provide the Commission with technical and logistical support, should the Commission wish to make use of that support.
records.political_signal: Signals readiness of UN peacekeeping assets to assist in election logistics if requested.
records.policy_implication: Maintains UN mandate support optionality despite host government preference for self-funding.

records.record_text: President Kabila underscored that elections were an internal affair and reiterated his decision to organize the elections without international support 'as a matter of principle', stating that past assistance had created 'havoc'.
records.actor_source: President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
records.political_signal: Rejects foreign electoral oversight or direct logistical dependency.
records.policy_implication: Limits direct MONUSCO operational role in election delivery unless requested.

records.record_text: Council members insisted on the need to reach a consensus over contentious issues, such as the use of voting machines and the voter registry, and advocated the full implementation of the 31 December 2016 political agreement, including the opening of the political space, respect for human rights, freedom of expression and the right to manifest.
records.actor_target: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
records.political_signal: Urges host authorities to build political consensus and open democratic space ahead of polls.
records.policy_implication: Links electoral legitimacy directly to political space and confidence-building implementation.

records.record_text: Council members called upon the Government to facilitate the entry of MONUSCO arms and ammunition into the Democratic Republic of the Congo to ensure the force is fully equipped to implement its mandate with regard to the protection of civilians.
records.actor_target: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
records.political_signal: Demands removal of administrative and logistical blockades on MONUSCO military equipment.
records.policy_implication: Critical for operational readiness of peacekeeping force in civilian protection operations.

records.record_text: The Government reproached MONUSCO for violating fundamental principles such as host country sovereignty, operating outside mandate limits, and failing to systematically coordinate patrols with national authorities, suggesting a review of collaboration in light of emerging threats such as terrorism in Beni.
records.actor_source: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
records.political_signal: Signals friction between host state and peacekeeping mission over operational autonomy.
records.policy_implication: Points toward upcoming pressure to reconfigure or review MONUSCO's status and presence.

records.record_text: Security Council members expressed concern that conditions for credible elections were not yet in place and asked what steps the Government intended to take to address the situation in a timely manner.
records.political_signal: Highlights international skepticism regarding technical and political preparation for elections.
records.policy_implication: Urges rapid government corrective measures to avoid post-election contested outcomes.

records.record_text: Delegates of the political opposition stressed that conditions for inclusive, free and transparent elections were not met due to persistent insecurity, CENI subservience to government authorities, controversies surrounding voting machines and the voter registry, and the exclusion of key candidates.
records.political_signal: Demonstrates deep opposition distrust in state institutions managing the election.
records.policy_implication: Increases risk of election rejection or political crises post-vote.

records.record_text: The opposition delegates confirmed that they would not boycott the elections and that they would soon agree on a unique candidate with a single programme.
records.political_signal: Signals commitment to democratic participation despite procedural complaints.
records.policy_implication: Ensures political opposition presence on the ballot on 23 December.

records.record_text: Female candidates expressed concerns about ongoing sexual and gender-based violence, discrimination, and political intimidation, noting that women faced extra challenges in conflict areas and constituted only 12 per cent of total candidates.
records.political_signal: Emphasizes systemic barriers and security threats limiting women's political participation.
records.policy_implication: Requires gender-sensitive security measures and protective support during campaigning.

records.record_text: CENCO urged the Security Council to engage CENI to seek consensus on voting machines or revert to ballot papers, clarify voter registry irregularities, invite international observers, and cooperate with MONUSCO on electoral kit logistics.
records.political_signal: Provides technical and compromise recommendations from an influential mediator to prevent electoral deadlock.
records.policy_implication: Offers a realistic framework for confidence-building measures before polling day.

records.record_text: CENCO advised against a postponement of the elections, arguing that this would create additional challenges, and called for a joint MONUSCO-government plan to secure the national territory during the electoral process.
records.political_signal: Warns against delays while calling for combined security guarantees for elections.
records.policy_implication: Reenforces strict adherence to the December 23 deadline backed by joint security arrangements.

records.record_text: Representatives of civil society organizations assessed that holding elections within the current climate of mistrust and persisting divergences could exacerbate the prospect of chaotic elections and recommended UN sanctions against political actors to end impunity.
records.political_signal: Warns of potential destabilization and demands punitive international pressure against spoilers.
records.policy_implication: Supports consideration of targeted sanctions against political actors violating rights or derailing process.

records.record_text: Civil society representatives from eastern DRC denounced continuing insecurity, armed militia recruitment of youth, and sexual abuse of women, expressing frustration that MONUSCO and its Intervention Brigade had failed to effectively neutralize armed groups in Beni.
records.political_signal: Reflects community dissatisfaction with peacekeeping force effectiveness in active conflict zones.
records.policy_implication: Calls for strengthening MONUSCO operational posture and community alert networks.

records.record_text: The United Nations country team suggested that the MONUSCO exit strategy be considered as a reconfiguration of the presence of the United Nations rather than a simple transfer of tasks, utilizing the humanitarian-development-peace nexus.
records.political_signal: Advocates long-term structural transition of UN engagement beyond peacekeeping.
records.policy_implication: Guides planning for MONUSCO transition, capacity building, and sustainable handover to UNCT/state.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Afghanistan, 12–15 January 2018

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Political Engagement and Situation Assessment Mission
main_risks: Continued high levels of security incidents and record civilian casualties driven by Taliban and ISIL-KP attacks
Political fragility, widespread public mistrust, and potential destabilization surrounding delayed parliamentary and presidential elections
Presence of cross-border safe havens and foreign terrorist fighters exacerbating regional volatility
Illicit drug trade and nexus between criminal networks, corruption, and insurgent financing
main_commitments: Government commitment to prioritizing security sector reform, particularly within the Ministries of Defence and Interior
Government commitment to holding credible parliamentary and district council elections in 2018 and presidential elections in 2019
SC commitment to constructively supporting regional approaches linking security and economic development
main_policy_signals: Reiteration of Security Council support for an inclusive, Afghan-led and Afghan-owned peace process
Emphasis on full and effective participation of women across political and peacebuilding processes
Strong encouragement of regional connectivity and 'One United Nations' coherence to optimize aid effectiveness and regional stability
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Afghanistan from 12 to 15 January 2018 reviewed the complex security, political, and socioeconomic challenges facing the National Unity Government. The mission emphasized that long-term stability requires an Afghan-led political process, timely and credible elections, robust security sector reform, and enhanced regional economic connectivity. Security Council members reaffirmed firm international support while urging greater national political unity, anti-corruption progress, and strategic UN system integration.

activities.activity_description: Safety briefing conducted by the UN Department of Safety and Security
Meeting with senior leadership and staff of the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA)
Meeting with senior Afghan security officials, including the National Security Adviser, Minister of Defence, Minister of the Interior, and Director General of NDS
Meeting with the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Afghanistan
Dinner hosted by Chief Executive Officer Abdullah Abdullah at the Ministry for Foreign Affairs
Meeting with President Mohammad Ashraf Ghani, Cabinet Ministers, and senior government officials
Meeting with Chief Executive Officer Abdullah Abdullah and senior officials
Thematic session on connectivity and infrastructure with senior presidential advisers and cabinet ministers
Lunch meeting with members of the Independent Election Commission (IEC) and Electoral Complaints Commission (ECC)
Thematic session on peace and reconciliation with leadership of the High Peace Council and security heads
Thematic session on the economy, development, refugees, and anti-corruption with Cabinet officials
Meeting on parliamentary affairs with the Speakers of the Wolesi Jirga and Meshrano Jirga and Minister of Parliamentary Affairs
Security briefing by the Commander of the NATO-led Resolute Support Mission
Meeting on women's empowerment with First Lady Rula Ghani and staff from the Office of the First Lady
Discussion session with representatives of main political parties
Meeting on human rights and civil society with AIHRC, Afghan Women's Network, and FEFA
Dinner hosted by President Mohammad Ashraf Ghani with government leadership, diplomatic corps, and UN leadership

records.record_text: The members of the Council voiced concern about the continued security incidents and indiscriminate attacks on civilians, which had reached record numbers, the growing presence of Taliban militants and fighters affiliated to Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant-Khorasan Province (ISIL-KP), in particular in the north and the east of the country, and the use of increasingly violent tactics that had the potential to deepen ethnic and sectarian tensions.
records.political_signal: Consensus concern over deteriorating security and civilian casualties
records.policy_implication: Highlights urgent need for comprehensive counter-terrorism and civilian protection measures

records.record_text: The Council members expressed support for Mr. Ghani’s efforts to reform the security sector and for greater international and regional cooperation in countering transnational terrorism, the movement of foreign terrorist fighters, extremism and criminal networks, including those involved in drug-trafficking.
records.political_signal: Endorsement of government security reforms and cross-border anti-terror cooperation
records.policy_implication: Encourages donor and regional backing for Afghan security sector reform

records.record_text: The world faced an emerging fifth wave of violence, forming a nexus between transnational terrorism and criminal networks, including drug-traffickers, exacerbated by State sponsorship of non-State armed groups.
records.political_signal: Afghan government views non-state armed groups as state-sponsored global threats
records.policy_implication: Calls for global military state-building strategies against state-sponsored terror

records.record_text: Mr. Abdullah stressed that State-sponsored terrorism in the pursuit of specific national interests could no longer be tolerated. There was consensus in the national unity Government on the need to pursue good relations with the country’s neighbours... Nonetheless, the status quo remained unchanged and the persons whom the Afghan security forces were fighting lived outside Afghanistan.
records.political_signal: Call out of foreign sanctuaries for insurgents operating in Afghanistan
records.policy_implication: Demands international pressure on regional states hosting armed militants

records.record_text: The officials said that the Taliban, including the Haqqani Network, had about 30,000 to 35,000 fighters, who were focused primarily on Afghanistan... A further 7,500 fighters had reportedly escaped military operations conducted against them in Pakistan and relocated to Afghanistan, while between 1,200 and 1,700 foreign fighters from groups with links to Al-Qaida... had come from neighbouring countries.
records.actor_source: Afghan Security Officials (NSA Atmar / DG NDS Stanekzai)
records.political_signal: Quantification of insurgent strength and cross-border terrorist movements
records.policy_implication: Provides intelligence baseline on armed group sizes and origins

records.record_text: General Nicholson said that military operations were not a solution in themselves but were conducted in support of an eventual political solution to the conflict... Once the Government had regained control of 80 per cent of the territory, the Taliban would have more incentive to join peace talks, especially if such talks were accompanied by a crackdown on sanctuaries.
records.actor_source: Commander of NATO Resolute Support Mission (General Nicholson)
records.political_signal: Military pressure aimed at driving Taliban to political negotiations
records.policy_implication: Aligns military strategy with political settlement prerequisites

records.record_text: Council members noted with concern the lack of tangible results in the peace process with the Taliban and underlined the need for negotiations between them and the Government. They concurred that there could be no solution to the conflict in Afghanistan in the absence of a political process
records.political_signal: Reaffirmation that conflict can only be resolved politically, not militarily
records.policy_implication: Prioritizes diplomatic and political framework for conflict resolution

records.record_text: Council members urged Mr. Ghani and Mr. Abdullah to maintain unity in the Government, which it needed in order to be able to deliver to the people, and reiterated the importance of holding free, fair, transparent and inclusive elections according to the agreed upon timetable.
records.political_signal: Strong Council backing for government cohesion and strict election timelines
records.policy_implication: Conditions political support on institutional stability and democratic credibility

records.record_text: Mr. Ghani and other participants welcomed the robust involvement of the United Nations and the international community, in particular in terms of monitoring, but were critical of the electoral support, which had not created sufficient capacity and had included very poor advice, provided by the United Nations thus far.
records.actor_source: President Mohammad Ashraf Ghani / Afghan Officials
records.political_signal: Afghan leadership discontent with UN technical electoral assistance
records.policy_implication: Requires review and quality improvement of UN technical support for elections

records.record_text: Doubts were rife about the capacity of the electoral management bodies and about the electoral timeline. A comprehensive election plan, including security and logistics measures, was needed and the electoral management bodies must be made more sustainable.
records.actor_source: Free and Fair Election Forum of Afghanistan (Yousuf Rashid)
records.political_signal: Civil society mistrust in election management readiness
records.policy_implication: Urges immediate security and operational planning for voter registration and polling

records.record_text: Ms. Samar briefed the Council members on the human rights situation... She also deplored the continuing culture of impunity, in particular with regard to violence against women.
records.political_signal: Highlighting persistent structural impunity for human rights violations and gender violence
records.policy_implication: Demands legal reform and accountability mechanisms for rights abuses

records.record_text: Although the Government emphasized the importance of development assistance in promoting stability in Afghanistan, discussions revealed a preference for a new paradigm, based not just on aid but rather, in particular, on increasing investment opportunities for trade, infrastructure, energy exchanges, market solutions and connectivity.
records.actor_source: Government of Afghanistan / Security Council Mission
records.political_signal: Shift from aid dependency towards economic self-reliance and commercial trade
records.policy_implication: Encourages donor transit investment in infrastructure and cross-border energy projects

records.record_text: Council members emphasized the importance of integration between Afghanistan and the neighbouring region. Connectivity would not only bring economic benefits but also contribute to stability.
records.political_signal: Linking Central Asian economic connectivity directly to Afghan peace
records.policy_implication: Promotes UN and regional support for trade corridors and infrastructure

records.record_text: Mr. Ghani reiterated his request for increased on-budget assistance and implementation of the 'One United Nations' initiative. He said that he had requested the United Nations country team to review its model of assistance, which did not support national ownership.
records.political_signal: Demand for UN reform in Afghanistan to shift towards direct budget support and harmonized operations
records.policy_implication: Requires UN Agencies, Funds, and Programmes to align under 'One UN' framework

records.record_text: Mr. Abdullah asked the Council to address the issues of safe havens and cross-border violations and to implement the sanctions regime more rigorously.
records.political_signal: Call for UN Security Council sanctions enforcement against external support networks
records.policy_implication: Encourages UNSC Sanctions Committees to review listings and enforcement

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Ethiopia, 6–8 September 2017

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Joint Consultative Meeting / UN-AU Partnership Engagement
main_risks: Premature AMISOM drawdown reversing security gains in Somalia against Al-Shabaab
Continued violence, slow implementation of the 2015 peace agreement, and worsening humanitarian crisis in South Sudan
Recruitment and regrouping of Boko Haram in Lake Chad Basin due to socioeconomic, political, and climate-related root causes
Unpredictable and ad hoc financing for African Union peace support operations
main_commitments: Support for the Joint UN-AU Framework for Enhanced Partnership in Peace and Security
Predictable, flexible, and sustainable funding for AMISOM accompanied by enhanced command, control, and accountability
Full support for the IGAD-led revitalization process and early deployment of the Regional Protection Force in South Sudan
Integration of UN-AU working modalities, including consideration of joint field missions and joint messaging
main_policy_signals: AMISOM drawdown must be systematic and conditions-based, aligned with Somali security capacity
There is no military solution to the South Sudan crisis; political dialogue and IGAD revitalization are essential
Addressing crisis dynamics in the Lake Chad Basin requires a comprehensive approach addressing climate change, poverty, and root causes
Recourse to UN assessed contributions for AU peace support operations requires compliance frameworks on human rights, financial transparency, and conduct
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Ethiopia from 6 to 8 September 2017 comprised the eleventh annual joint consultative meeting with the Peace and Security Council of the African Union at AU headquarters in Addis Ababa. The mission focused on strengthening the strategic partnership between the UN and AU, addressing key regional peace and security crises—specifically in Somalia, South Sudan, and the Lake Chad Basin—and examining mechanisms for predictable financing of AU peace support operations as well as post-conflict reconstruction and peacebuilding.

activities.activity_description: Meeting on 6 September 2017 with senior UN officials (SRSG to AU Haile Menkerios, Special Envoy Nicholas Haysom, SRSG David Shearer, and SRSG Michael Keating) to exchange views on regional and country-specific situations.
Meeting on 7 September 2017 with the Prime Minister of Ethiopia, Hailemariam Dessalegn, and Special Envoy Berhane Gebre-Christos regarding Ethiopian perspectives on regional security.

Meeting on 7 September 2017 with the AU Commissioner for Peace and Security and the Commissioner for Political Affairs to discuss operationalizing the UN-AU strategic partnership and AU institutional reforms.
Second informal joint seminar on 7 September 2017 between UNSC and AU PSC members to discuss partnership, financing for AU peace support operations, and post-conflict reconstruction.
Eleventh annual joint consultative meeting between UNSC and AU PSC members on 8 September 2017 addressing Somalia, South Sudan, and the Lake Chad Basin.

actors_met.actor_name: Haile Menkerios, Special Representative of the Secretary-General to the African Union and Head of UNOAU
Nicholas Haysom, Special Envoy of the Secretary-General for Sudan and South Sudan
David Shearer, Special Representative of the Secretary-General for South Sudan and Head of UNMISS
Michael Keating, Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Somalia and Head of UNSOM
Hailemariam Dessalegn, Prime Minister of Ethiopia
African Union Peace and Security Council (AU PSC)
AU Commissioner for Peace and Security
AU Commissioner for Political Affairs

records.record_text: The co-chairs of the meeting made parallel calls for joint field missions and harmonization of the programmes of work of the two Councils, expressing hope that the consultations would add more value to their work.
records.actor_source: Co-Chairs of the UNSC-AU PSC Meeting
records.actor_target: UN Security Council and AU Peace and Security Council
records.political_signal: Call for institutional harmonization and joint operational deployment between UN and AU bodies.
records.policy_implication: Potential development of aligned annual schedules and joint field visits.

records.record_text: While members of both Councils acknowledged the gains made by the African Union Mission in Somalia (AMISOM) in the Al-Shabaab counteroffensive... the discussion on a possible AMISOM drawdown emphasized the importance that it be systematic and based on conditions so as to avoid a reversal of the gains achieved so far, and that it should reflect the need for Somali military and police forces to assume greater responsibility for security.
records.actor_source: UN Security Council and AU Peace and Security Council Members
records.political_signal: AMISOM drawdown must be strictly conditions-based rather than timeline-driven.
records.policy_implication: Troop transition plans must explicitly link to benchmarked capacity-building of Somali national security forces.

records.record_text: In the light of the continued attacks by Al-Shabaab, they expressed the commitment of the Security Council to continue supporting the operations and stressed the need to improve the operational readiness of the troops. In that regard, Security Council members called for predictable, flexible and sustainable funding for AMISOM, accompanied by efficient, effective, accountable and transparent counteroffensive operations, as well as effective oversight, command and control and joint planning.
records.political_signal: Funding support for AMISOM is tied to structural reforms in operational readiness, joint planning, and financial transparency.
records.policy_implication: Requirements for strengthened oversight frameworks for AMISOM.

records.record_text: The Peace and Security Council underlined the need for enablers, multipliers and related logistical support for AMISOM... The Peace and Security Council stressed that implementation of the Somali national development plan was a prerequisite for lasting peace and security.
records.political_signal: AU demand for critical military enablers and holistic development backing prior to security transition.
records.policy_implication: Need to mobilize specialized military assets and long-term economic development funding for Somalia.

records.record_text: Members of the Security Council and the Peace and Security Council emphasized the importance of close collaboration between the African Union, the United Nations and the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD). They also highlighted the need for unconditional, inclusive and genuine political dialogue and for full support to the IGAD-led revitalization process towards full implementation of the 2015 peace agreement.
records.actor_source: UN Security Council and AU Peace and Security Council Members
records.political_signal: Unified international alignment behind IGAD leadership for peace agreement revitalization.
records.policy_implication: Coordinated diplomatic pressure on South Sudanese stakeholders to participate in the revitalization process.

records.record_text: Members of the Security Council expressed regret over the slow implementation of the peace agreement and the growing apprehension in South Sudan... Some stressed that it would be premature to hold elections in 2018 as envisaged... They also called for the full deployment of the regional protection force and noted that there was no military solution to the crisis and that genuine dialogue could not take place while fighting was ongoing.
records.actor_target: South Sudanese Parties and Transitional Government
records.political_signal: Explicit warning that elections cannot proceed under present conflict conditions and that fighting must cease.
records.policy_implication: Prioritization of immediate cessation of hostilities and Regional Protection Force deployment over premature electoral processes.

records.record_text: The Peace and Security Council noted with satisfaction the similar language used by both Councils on the situation in South Sudan. It highlighted the critical importance of the full deployment of the regional protection force, which should be operational without delay.
records.actor_target: UN Security Council and Government of South Sudan
records.political_signal: AU support for immediate and unhindered operationalization of the Regional Protection Force.
records.policy_implication: Pressuring host authorities to remove obstacles to UNMISS and RPF operationalization.

records.record_text: Based on their respective visits to the region, members of both Councils noted that while the Multinational Joint Task Force and other associated operations had weakened Boko Haram, the situation remained fertile for violent extremists to recruit and regroup, unless the political, socioeconomic and environmental root causes were addressed.
records.actor_source: UN Security Council and AU Peace and Security Council Members
records.political_signal: Military victories against Boko Haram are unsustainable without comprehensive non-military responses.
records.policy_implication: Shift towards integrated regional stabilization strategies targeting root structural causes.

records.record_text: Underlining the efforts of countries of the region to tackle the crisis, members of the Security Council called for support to be provided to them, complementing reactive humanitarian and military measures with efforts towards long-term sustainable development. Some members underscored a clear link between climate change and the crisis in the area, within the context of the population's vulnerability.
records.political_signal: Recognition of climate change and environmental degradation as structural drivers of conflict and instability.
records.policy_implication: Integration of climate risk analysis and long-term resilience projects into stabilization programming.

records.record_text: The Peace and Security Council called for support from the Security Council to the planned conference of the Lake Chad Basin Commission on the development of a regional stabilization strategy, including with a view to promoting the resilience of local communities.
records.political_signal: AU request for UN endorsement and assistance for LCBC regional stabilization initiatives.
records.policy_implication: Formal UN backing and technical support for the LCBC Regional Stabilization Strategy.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Mali, Guinea-Bissau and Senegal

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Political engagement, peace agreement implementation review, mandate review, and regional security assessment
main_risks: Deterioration of the security situation and expansion of violent attacks, terrorism, and transnational organized crime in central and northern Mali
Delays in the cantonment, DDR, decentralization, and interim administration processes threatening the implementation of the Malian peace agreement
Protracted political impasse, institutional instability, and governance paralysis in Guinea-Bissau resulting from executive-legislative disputes
Operational overstretch, resource deficits, and logistical/equipment shortages facing MINUSMA
Financial shortfalls threatening the continuation of ECOMIB in Guinea-Bissau
main_commitments: Agreement by signatory parties in Mali to establish a new implementation timeline for the peace agreement
Commitment by Guinea-Bissau national stakeholders to seek political solutions within constitutional boundaries and respect judicial decisions
Operationalization of the merger of UNOWA and OSES into UNOWAS
Commitment by international partners and regional mechanisms to step up information-sharing, border security, and counter-terrorism coordination
main_policy_signals: Urgent call for concrete, swift, and inclusive implementation of the Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation in Mali
Support for reviewing MINUSMA's role, posture, and capacities to adapt to an increasingly asymmetric and complex security environment
Strong signal to Guinea-Bissau leadership to preserve democratic gains, abide by the rule of law, and resolve political grievances through inclusive dialogue
Emphasis on regional, multi-dimensional conflict prevention strategies to address the root causes of instability and violent extremism across the Sahel and West Africa
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to West Africa evaluated peace and security challenges across Mali, Guinea-Bissau, and Senegal. In Mali, the mission emphasized the urgent imperative for signatory parties to accelerate the concrete implementation of the 2015 Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation amidst growing asymmetric terrorist threats and MINUSMA operational challenges. In Guinea-Bissau, the Council addressed a deteriorating political impasse between the President, Prime Minister, Parliament, and political parties, calling for constitutional adherence, rule of law, and inclusive dialogue. In Senegal, the mission engaged regional actors and UN leadership to reinforce subregional counter-terrorism, conflict prevention, and the merger of UN offices into UNOWAS.

records.record_text: The President of Mali highlighted recent steps taken to implement institutional reforms, such as the creation of two new regions in northern Mali and the launch of a constitutional reform process, and announced plans for signatory parties to agree within two months on a new timeline for peace agreement implementation.
records.political_signal: Demonstrates government initiative toward advancing structural elements of the peace agreement.
records.policy_implication: Establishes an updated benchmark timeline for monitoring Malian peace agreement progress.

records.record_text: The President of Mali called for an extensive review of the mandate of MINUSMA, including the strengthening of its capacities, so that it would be adapted to the current context in which MINUSMA had become a prime target of terrorist attacks.
records.political_signal: High-level host government demand for enhancing mission force protection and counter-threat posture.
records.policy_implication: Informs the upcoming strategic review and mandate renewal of MINUSMA under Council consideration.

records.record_text: The Prime Minister of Mali noted that delays in cantonment and disarmament, demobilization and reintegration processes could cause elements of the signatory armed groups to be tempted to join the ranks of terrorist groups.
records.political_signal: Highlights operational risks where delays in formal security processes feed violent extremism.
records.policy_implication: Requires urgent acceleration of technical cantonment and DDR financing and mechanisms.

records.record_text: CMA and Platform representatives highlighted the risk of further delays and noted that, without progress on security sector reform and further clarity on DDR and integration, further steps relating to the defence and security elements of the peace agreement would be difficult.
records.political_signal: Signals conditional participation of non-state armed groups on security guarantees and SSR political decisions.
records.policy_implication: Underlines the necessity of functional National Council on SSR to unlock progress on combatant lists and cantonment.

records.record_text: MINUSMA representatives stressed the importance of addressing deficits in training and equipment, in particular armoured vehicles, urgently and called for slow or ineffective budgetary and administrative procedures to be reviewed due to their negative impact on operations and security.
records.political_signal: Internal UN assessment identifying systemic operational bottlenecks hindering mission fulfillment.
records.policy_implication: Directs UN Secretariat and TCCs/PCCs to rectify equipment shortfalls and streamline administrative procedures.

records.record_text: The members of the Security Council expressed concern at the lack of inclusiveness of the Malian peace process, especially regarding the inclusion and representation of women, disenfranchised young people, and individuals at risk of recruitment by negative forces.
records.political_signal: Council priority on broad social inclusion as vital for sustainable peace and preventing conflict relapse.
records.policy_implication: Requires monitoring mechanisms to enforce minimum quota laws and integrate civil society in implementation bodies.

records.record_text: The members of the Security Council expressed serious concern at the deterioration of the security situation in central and northern Mali, strongly condemned violent attacks against civilians, government institutions, armed groups, MINUSMA, and Operation Barkhane, and discussed establishing a structured coalition against insecurity.
records.political_signal: Reaffirms UNSC zero tolerance for violence while contemplating improved operational coordination mechanisms.
records.policy_implication: Prompts potential revision of MINUSMA's mandate to support enhanced counter-terrorism coordination or posture.

records.record_text: In Guinea-Bissau, Security Council members voiced concern about continuing political instability and appealed to main conflicting parties to resolve grievances, show flexibility, respect the rule of law, and finalize the cabinet through dialogue.
records.political_signal: Clear Council call to prevent political infighting from unravelling post-2014 democratic and financial gains.
records.policy_implication: Sets expectations for national dialogue and adherence to constitutional judicial rulings.

records.record_text: The President of Guinea-Bissau asserted that the current crisis was political in nature requiring a political solution, warned that relying on courts alone would risk politicizing the judiciary, and pledged to abide by Supreme Court decisions.
records.political_signal: Reflects executive perspective favoring negotiated political compromise over purely judicial resolution.
records.policy_implication: Highlights the delicate balance between executive prerogative, parliamentary majorities, and judicial review.

records.record_text: The Prime Minister and National Assembly Speaker in Guinea-Bissau justified the expulsion and seat removal of 15 PAIGC parliamentarians who had abstained from supporting the Government's programme, maintaining that legal and statutory procedures were strictly followed.
records.actor_source: Prime Minister & Assembly Speaker of Guinea-Bissau
records.political_signal: Defends parliamentary actions while accusing presidential interference of driving the impasse.
records.policy_implication: Demonstrates deep institutional divide over legislative mandates impeding parliament functionality.

records.record_text: The Security Council members observed that Guinea-Bissau political parties were deeply divided and emphasized that political stability, respecting the rule of law, combating impunity, and functioning democratic organs were mandatory to meet the people's needs.
records.political_signal: Direct warning to political leaders that ongoing friction imperils socio-economic development and stability.
records.policy_implication: Reinforces mandate of UNIOGBIS to offer good offices and support rule of law consolidation.

records.record_text: The Special Representative of the Secretary-General for West Africa noted growing subregional awareness of terrorism vulnerabilities and highlighted UNOWAS good offices efforts supporting peaceful electoral processes in Benin, the Niger, Cabo Verde, and Senegal.
records.political_signal: Demonstrates the efficacy of UN preventative diplomacy and regional election monitoring.
records.policy_implication: Validates Council decision to merge UNOWA and OSES into a unified UNOWAS structure.

records.record_text: President Macky Sall of Senegal suggested that Guinea-Bissau's semi-presidential system was the root cause of recurrent crises due to multiple power centers, recommending future constitutional reform while highlighting the financial strain facing ECOMIB.
records.political_signal: Regional leadership diagnostic pointing to structural institutional flaws requiring constitutional remedies.
records.policy_implication: Urges international financial support to prevent premature drawdown of ECOMIB stabilization forces.

records.record_text: The Security Council members acknowledged that security threats, transnational organized crime, and violent extremism across West Africa and the Sahel require multidimensional approaches addressing root socio-economic causes, social services, and youth opportunities.
records.political_signal: Holistic Council vision connecting security measures with economic development to eliminate recruitment grounds for terrorism.
records.policy_implication: Calls for mobilizing adequate international resources for the UN Integrated Strategy for the Sahel and regional mechanisms.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to the Central African Republic, Ethiopia and Burundi, including the African Union

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Implementation Review and Political Engagement Mission
main_risks: Fragile security situation and continued occupation of areas by ex-Séléka and anti-Balaka armed groups in Central African Republic.
Financial deficits and operational delays threatening electoral timetables in Central African Republic and Burundi.
Contested presidential third-term candidacy in Burundi threatening stability and the Arusha Agreement framework.
Shrinking political space, intimidation by Imbonerakure youth group, and human rights violations in Burundi.
Regional security threats posed by Boko Haram, LRA, FDLR, and Al-Shabaab.
main_commitments: Security Council consideration of increased troop/resource allocations for MINUSCA.
Transitional authorities in Central African Republic committed to inclusive political process, local consultations, and Bangui Forum.
Establishment of Special Criminal Court and passage of draft legislation in Central African Republic.
Enhanced strategic coordination between UN Security Council and AU Peace and Security Council, including conflict prevention mechanisms.
Burundian Government commitment to hold elections and cooperate with MENUB.

Imperative of ending impunity and establishing national accountability mechanisms in CAR and South Sudan.
Urgent need for Chapter VII endorsement and sustainable international funding for the Multinational Joint Task Force against Boko Haram.
Absolute necessity of maintaining an open, inclusive political space and adhering to constitutional/Arusha frameworks in Burundi.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to the Central African Republic, Ethiopia (African Union), and Burundi evaluated critical political transitions and regional security dynamics. In CAR, the mission focused on MINUSCA's deployment, protection of civilians, extension of State authority, disarmament, and preparations for the Bangui Forum and national elections. In Addis Ababa, joint consultations with the AU Peace and Security Council reinforced the UN-AU partnership on major regional crises including Boko Haram, Great Lakes, Mali, Somalia, and South Sudan. In Burundi, the mission addressed heightened political tensions, human rights concerns, shrinking political space, and controversies surrounding presidential term limits ahead of the 2015 elections, urging adherence to the spirit of the Arusha Agreement.
