mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Mali, 1-3 February 2014

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Peace process support, implementation review, and UN mission deployment assessment
main_risks: Deepening lack of trust and potential radicalization/re-arming of northern armed group factions due to delays in launching inclusive peace talks.
Persistent terrorist threat and rural insecurity exacerbated by MINUSMA deployment delays and lack of critical air assets.
Growing civil society dissatisfaction regarding impunity for past human rights abuses and executive interference in judicial processes.
Potential exploitation of the political vacuum by spoilers as Operation Serval draws down.
main_commitments: Malian authorities committed to involving civil society and women's organizations in national reconciliation and inclusive dialogue.
Malian Government earmarked CFA 35 billion in 2013-2014 budget to rehabilitate public infrastructure in northern Mali.
Reform of the Dialogue and Reconciliation Commission into the Truth, Justice and Reconciliation Commission to address human rights abuses since 1961.
Signatory armed groups (MNLA and HCUA) reaffirmed willingness to canton combatants and disarm upon signature of a comprehensive peace accord.
main_policy_signals: Urgent call for the immediate launch of inclusive and credible intra-Malian peace negotiations without preconditions and within a defined timetable.
Reaffirmation that cantonment is the initial step, while full disarmament will occur following the conclusion of a comprehensive peace agreement.
Emphasis that responsibility for law and order must reside with civilian police rather than military forces.
Call for international partners and UN agencies to address humanitarian funding gaps and support long-term development to tackle root causes of instability.
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Mali from 1 to 3 February 2014 focused on reviving the stalled political process under the Ouagadougou preliminary agreement and evaluating MINUSMA's deployment. The Council urged all parties to launch inclusive peace negotiations immediately without preconditions, clarifying that cantonment precedes full disarmament upon a comprehensive peace agreement. The mission underscored the urgency of expediting MINUSMA's operational deployment—particularly procuring critical air assets—to fill security gaps in northern Mali as French Operation Serval transitions primarily to counter-terrorism. Furthermore, stakeholders emphasized that sustainable stability requires addressing governance and development deficits, restoring state authority, and ensuring accountability for human rights abuses.

records.record_text: The primary purpose of the Security Council mission was to reiterate the Council's urgent call for the launch of an inclusive and credible negotiation process after a halt of several months in the convening of the two implementation bodies established pursuant to the Ouagadougou preliminary agreement—the Monitoring and Evaluation Committee and the Mixed Technical Commission on Security.
records.political_signal: The Security Council demands the immediate resumption of peace negotiations.
records.policy_implication: Re-activation of implementation bodies established by the Ouagadougou Agreement.

records.record_text: Signatory armed groups (MNLA and HCUA) called for full implementation of the Ouagadougou preliminary agreement, reiterating willingness to canton combatants and disarm upon signature of a comprehensive peace accord, and proposed that Algeria join existing dialogue mechanisms in a neutral location.
records.political_signal: Armed groups condition disarmament on a finalized comprehensive peace accord.
records.policy_implication: Mediation structure requires coordination between Algerian initiative and Ouagadougou mechanisms.

records.record_text: Adherent groups (MAA and CMFPR) expressed frustration that they were excluded from the Mixed Technical Commission on Security and had not been assigned cantonment sites, insisting on the multi-ethnic character of northern Mali and their necessary inclusion in negotiations.
records.actor_target: Mixed Technical Commission on Security / MINUSMA
records.political_signal: Exclusion of non-signatory groups risks creating political spoilers.
records.policy_implication: Current members of the Mixed Technical Commission must agree to expand membership.

records.record_text: Civil society organizations pressed for inclusive dialogue not to be restricted to armed groups but to include conflict victims and ordinary citizens in Mali, so as not to reward armed elements for abuses committed against civilians.
records.political_signal: Peace process must incorporate public participation and transitional justice.
records.policy_implication: Government and UN must facilitate civil society access to peace talks.

records.record_text: President Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta stated that the Malian Government should take ownership of the reconciliation process with any new agreement signed in Mali, and stressed that full disarmament of armed groups should precede the comprehensive negotiation process.
records.political_signal: Government insists on national sovereignty and pre-negotiation disarmament.
records.policy_implication: Divergence between Government demand for full disarmament prior to negotiations and armed groups' insistence on cantonment first.

records.record_text: The Prime Minister briefed the mission on preparatory steps scheduled for February 2014, including MINUSMA-supported workshops on lessons learned, cantonment, DDR, and return of state administration, alongside government consultations with civil society.
records.political_signal: Government is preparing operational road maps prior to launching full dialogue.
records.policy_implication: Technical workshops pave the ground for formal peace negotiations.

records.record_text: International members of the Monitoring and Evaluation Committee warned that the current lapse in implementing the preliminary agreement heightens the risk of further divisions among armed groups, re-armament, and exploitation by potential spoilers.
records.actor_source: Monitoring and Evaluation Committee International Members
records.political_signal: Political deadlock poses imminent security threats to fragile stability.
records.policy_implication: Urgent international pressure is required to break the political impasse.

records.record_text: The Security Council mission urged parties to engage without preconditions in inclusive talks immediately within a pre-established timetable, reaffirming that cantonment is the first step in disarmament and full disarmament takes place upon signature of a comprehensive peace agreement.
records.political_signal: Clarified international sequencing standard: cantonment during negotiations, disarmament post-agreement.
records.policy_implication: Sets clear baseline parameters to resolve sequencing disagreements between Government and armed groups.

records.record_text: Civil society representatives denounced the release of conflict-related prisoners and lifting of arrest warrants against former MPs as executive infringement on judicial independence, while calling along with armed groups for an international commission of inquiry.
records.political_signal: Executive political confidence-building measures clash with domestic demands for judicial accountability.
records.policy_implication: Need to balance short-term political concessions with long-term justice commitments.

records.record_text: The Malian Government renamed and reformed the Dialogue and Reconciliation Commission into the Truth, Justice and Reconciliation Commission, mandating it to investigate human rights abuses and violations committed since 1961 with civil society involvement.
records.political_signal: State commitment to institutionalized transitional justice.
records.policy_implication: UN and partners need to provide technical support to the newly established Commission.

records.record_text: Civil society and northern armed groups reported that MINUSMA was securing only major urban centres while rural civilians remained vulnerable to threats, while MINUSMA leadership stressed that lack of critical enablers such as helicopters severely curtailed deployment across northern Mali.
records.actor_target: Security Council Mission / UN Member States
records.political_signal: Protection of civilians gap in rural northern Mali due to missing military enablers.
records.policy_implication: UN Secretariat and Member States must urgently provide air assets and specialized military capabilities.

records.record_text: Malian and international interlocutors stressed that terrorist and jihadist groups retained significant capacity and aimed to regain control over northern Mali.
records.political_signal: Asymmetrical security threat persists despite formal military interventions.
records.policy_implication: Continued necessity of counter-terrorism operations parallel to UN stabilization operations.

records.record_text: The Serval Commander briefed that French forces would draw down and solely conduct counter-terrorism activities, leaving MINUSMA with lead responsibility for securing key population centres and protecting civilians in northern Mali.
records.political_signal: Transition of primary security burden in northern Mali from French forces to UN peacekeepers.
records.policy_implication: MINUSMA must accelerate operational readiness to absorb security responsibilities.

records.record_text: MINUSMA reported having only 5,910 of 11,200 authorized military personnel on the ground during the visit, projecting full operational capacity by June 2014, supported by 70-hectare land allocations from the Government for joint civil-military bases.
records.political_signal: Deployment is advancing but lagging behind mandate expectations.
records.policy_implication: Force generation efforts must be prioritized to reach full strength by mid-2014.

records.record_text: EUTM Mali and Serval provided positive feedback on three Malian army battalions trained in Koulikoro, but emphasized that security sector reform is a long-term endeavor, civilian police must manage law and order, and northern populations still distrust the national military.
records.political_signal: Military training alone is insufficient without broad governance reform and civil policing emphasis.
records.policy_implication: International community must sustain long-term engagement in Malian SSR beyond current military training scope.

records.record_text: The Prime Minister reported allocating CFA 35 billion in the 2013-2014 budget to rehabilitate northern infrastructure, while UN officials noted that 75 per cent of schools and 90 per cent of health centres in Gao had re-opened, though food insecurity remained acute.
records.actor_source: Prime Minister of Mali / UN Humanitarian Coordinator
records.political_signal: Gradual state administrative return is underway but basic humanitarian needs remain severe.
records.policy_implication: Sustained development funding needed alongside short-term humanitarian relief.

records.record_text: Civil society representatives emphasized that the northern crisis stemmed primarily from chronic underdevelopment and weak governance rather than underlying ethnic tensions, while President Keïta committed to a zero-tolerance policy on corruption.
records.political_signal: Sustainable peace requires addressing structural socio-economic neglect and corruption.
records.policy_implication: Donor assistance must target economic development, anti-corruption, and local governance initiatives.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, Uganda and Ethiopia (including the African Union)
mission_country_or_region: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, Uganda, Ethiopia, Great Lakes Region

mission_analytics.mission_subtype: Regional Peace, Security, and Strategic Partnership Assessment
main_risks: Destabilizing activities of foreign and domestic armed groups (M23, FDLR, ADF-NALU, LRA)
Persistent humanitarian crisis and displacement in eastern DRC
Weak state authority and slow security sector reform in the DRC
Regional interference, external support, and arms flow to illegal armed groups
Impunity for grave human rights violations, atrocities, and sexual violence
main_commitments: Full and good-faith implementation of the Peace, Security and Cooperation Framework for the DRC and the Region
Conclusion of the Kampala peace talks between the DRC Government and M23
Comprehensive Security Sector Reform (SSR) in the DRC
Phased transfer of appropriate MONUSCO tasks to the UN Country Team and DRC Government
Enhancement of the strategic partnership and cooperation mechanisms between the UN Security Council and the AU Peace and Security Council
main_policy_signals: Strict respect by all regional States for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and non-interference in the internal affairs of the DRC
Zero tolerance for assistance, harbouring, or tolerance of armed groups by any regional actor
Support for MONUSCO and its Force Intervention Brigade to neutralize all armed groups in eastern DRC while prioritizing civilian protection
Imperative of addressing the root political and structural causes of conflict alongside military actions
Ending impunity through comprehensive judicial reform, restrictive army integration, and accountability for human rights violations
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to the Great Lakes region and the African Union assessed regional conflict dynamics, evaluated implementation of resolution 2098 (2013) and the Peace, Security and Cooperation Framework, and reinforced strategic cooperation with the AU. The Council emphasized that durable peace in the eastern DRC requires an integrated approach: political dialogue and conclusion of the Kampala talks, complete neutralization of negative forces by MONUSCO and FARDC, strict observance of non-interference by neighbouring States, systemic security sector and judicial reforms, and enhanced regional economic integration.

activities.activity_description: Meeting with members of the European Union Political and Security Committee in Brussels en route to Kinshasa.
Meetings in Kinshasa with DRC President Joseph Kabila Kabange, Prime Minister Augustin Matata Ponyo Mapon, and key Cabinet Ministers.
Meeting in Kinshasa with DRC parliamentary leaders, including President of the Senate Leon Kengo wa Dongo and Speaker of the National Assembly Aubin Minaku.
Attendance at the closing ceremony of the DRC national consultations co-chaired by parliamentary leadership in the presence of President Kabila.
Detailed briefings and working lunch in Kinshasa with MONUSCO and the UN country team on resolution 2098 (2013) and task transfer planning.
Separate meetings in Goma with Governor of North Kivu Julien Paluku and representatives of civil society and humanitarian NGOs.
Site visit to Kibati towers near Goma to inspect positions from which M23 shelled Goma and receive briefings on joint operations and mandate implementation.
Field visit to Munigi camp for internally displaced persons in North Kivu to meet displaced civilians and humanitarian workers.
High-level meeting in Kigali with President of Rwanda Paul Kagame, Foreign Minister Louise Mushikiwabo, Defence Minister James Kabarebe, and Director of NISS Karenzi Karake.
Visit to the Mutobo demobilization centre in Rwanda to engage with former FDLR combatants undergoing demobilization and reintegration.
Visit to the Genocide Memorial in Kigali, Rwanda.
Update briefing at Entebbe airport on the status of the Kampala process between the DRC Government and M23.
Meeting in Kampala with President of Uganda Yoweri Kaguta Museveni and senior facilitation representative Cyrus Kiyonga.
Seventh annual joint consultative meeting between the UN Security Council and the African Union Peace and Security Council in Addis Ababa.
Meeting in Addis Ababa with Chairperson of the African Union Commission Nkosazana Dlamini Zuma.
Meeting in Addis Ababa with Prime Minister of Ethiopia and AU Chairperson Hailemariam Dessalegn.

records.record_text: The European Union reiterated its commitment to continue supporting the reconstruction of the Democratic Republic of the Congo while pursuing stabilization efforts in the eastern part of the country, identifying as a priority the conclusion of the talks in Kampala between the Government and M23.
records.actor_source: European Union Political and Security Committee
records.political_signal: Strong European Union backing for political negotiation in Kampala to clear the path for addressing conflict root causes.
records.policy_implication: Concluding the Kampala talks is essential to establishing the baseline conditions for eastern DRC stabilization.

records.record_text: There was agreement that the reform of the security sector was a precondition for establishing peace and stability in the country and eventually allowing MONUSCO to draw down.
records.actor_target: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
records.political_signal: MONUSCO drawdown is explicitly linked to measurable progress in national security sector reform.
records.policy_implication: DRC sovereign capability to maintain internal security is a prerequisite for MONUSCO exit.

records.record_text: The members of the Security Council called upon President Kabila to implement the national commitments made under the Framework and to intensify efforts to reform the security sector, consolidate State authority, make progress on decentralization and further the agenda of reconciliation, tolerance and democratization.
records.actor_target: President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
records.political_signal: Direct Security Council demand for domestic institutional reforms under the Peace, Security and Cooperation Framework.
records.policy_implication: DRC state credibility relies on parallel progress across security, political, administrative, and social tracks.

records.record_text: The Congolese Minister of Defence outlined that the Congolese rapid reaction force should be operational by 2020, while by 2025 the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo should be in a position to ensure the security of the country and its people independently.
records.actor_source: Minister of Defence of the DRC
records.political_signal: The DRC Government projects a long-term timeline (2020–2025) for full security self-reliance.
records.policy_implication: International security assistance and peacekeeping support will remain necessary over an extended timeframe.

records.record_text: President Kabila reiterated that the Government's position on amnesty was clear: there would be no impunity for those who committed serious violations of human rights and international humanitarian law, avoiding past mistakes of blanket amnesty and subsequent integration.
records.actor_source: President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
records.political_signal: Firm DRC refusal to grant blanket amnesties or automatic army integration to armed group leaders accused of atrocities.
records.policy_implication: Break from historical peace deal formulas that traded justice for short-term combatant integration.

records.record_text: The Security Council members emphasized the need for free, fair and transparent national and provincial elections to be accomplished within the constitutional time frame.
records.actor_target: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
records.political_signal: Strict adherence to constitutional electoral timelines is mandatory for international political legitimacy.
records.policy_implication: Electoral preparations must proceed without delay despite ongoing eastern security challenges.

records.record_text: The members of the Security Council expressed support for MONUSCO, recognizing that the Force Intervention Brigade was an effective tool that was already yielding tangible results, while stressing the need to find a political solution and address the root causes of the conflict.
records.political_signal: Validation of the offensive mandate of the Force Intervention Brigade coupled with the requirement for political resolution.
records.policy_implication: Military operations by the Force Intervention Brigade are necessary but insufficient without structural political solutions.

records.record_text: President Kabila stated that the Democratic Republic of the Congo was the only signatory of the Peace, Security and Cooperation Framework agreement that had taken action to implement its commitments, urging regional actors and the international community to make equal progress.
records.actor_source: President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
records.political_signal: DRC criticism of neighbouring countries for non-compliance with regional non-interference commitments.
records.policy_implication: Regional mistrust threatens the viability of the Peace, Security and Cooperation Framework.

records.record_text: Governor of North Kivu and civil society representatives expressed the view that the involvement of neighbouring States, particularly Rwanda and Uganda, through provision of arms, ammunition, and recruitment support, was the main cause of conflict in eastern DRC.
records.actor_source: Governor of North Kivu and Civil Society Representatives
records.political_signal: Local provincial leadership and civil society directly accuse neighbouring countries of fueling armed proxy conflict.
records.policy_implication: Addressing external state sponsorship is essential for local civilian protection in North Kivu.

records.record_text: President Kagame explained that FDLR remained a threat to Rwanda because of its ideology and sought the Council's support in pressing for MONUSCO to enact concrete measures to address the FDLR issue.
records.political_signal: Rwanda prioritizes the robust operational neutralization of FDLR by MONUSCO as a non-negotiable national security concern.
records.policy_implication: MONUSCO's Force Intervention Brigade must target FDLR with equal vigour to maintain regional credibility.

records.record_text: The members of the Security Council agreed that the MONUSCO Force Intervention Brigade should pursue all armed groups that posed a threat to the region and reiterated their call upon all countries in the region not to tolerate or provide assistance to armed groups.
records.political_signal: Unequivocal Security Council mandate for MONUSCO to target all armed groups neutrally and robustly.
records.policy_implication: Regional states must terminate all illicit channels of support to any armed faction in DRC.

records.record_text: President Kagame urged that the pursuit of justice in the region not be pursued selectively and that all perpetrators of atrocities be identified and prosecuted, sharing his view that Africa should have its own regional criminal court.
records.political_signal: Rwandan call for non-discriminatory international accountability and continental judicial autonomy.
records.policy_implication: Accountability mechanisms must encompass all combatant factions to avoid perceptions of victor's justice.

records.record_text: President Museveni shared his view that amnesty should be proposed to all except those who have committed crimes against humanity, describing conditional amnesty as a centerpiece for reconciliation.
records.political_signal: Ugandan advocacy for broad conditional amnesties to incentivize armed group demobilization.
records.policy_implication: Tension exists between pragmatic conflict resolution through amnesty and strict international justice norms.

records.record_text: President Museveni argued that integration of former combatants into the armed forces was first and foremost about security and peacebuilding, as alternative state power structures did not exist in the DRC.
records.political_signal: Ugandan perspective prioritizing army integration over exclusion to prevent renewed armed insurgency.
records.policy_implication: Clashes with Kinshasa's policy of restrictive integration and strict vetting.

records.record_text: President Museveni cautioned the Security Council against taking sides in Africa's conflicts, maintaining that by taking sides they had been part of the problem, and urged reliance on a 'holy trinity' alliance of national, regional and international actors.
records.political_signal: Criticism of UNSC interventionism and strong endorsement of regional leadership in dispute settlement.
records.policy_implication: UN Security Council decisions must align closely with regional mediation frameworks.

records.record_text: During the seventh annual joint consultative meeting, the UN Security Council and AU Peace and Security Council exchanged views on enhancing their strategic partnership, flexible application of subsidiarity, and improved synchronization of conflict interventions across Africa.
records.actor_source: UN Security Council and AU Peace and Security Council
records.actor_target: UN Security Council and AU Peace and Security Council
records.political_signal: Institutional commitment to strengthen UN-AU institutional alignment and division of labour.
records.policy_implication: Requires earlier joint consultations, harmonized field missions, and predictable funding support for AU-led peace operations.

records.record_text: Ethiopian Prime Minister Hailemariam Dessalegn emphasized that the conflict in the Democratic Republic of the Congo was not primarily a security problem but a political one requiring regional contribution to an internal solution.
records.political_signal: AU Chair's framing of the DRC crisis as fundamentally political rather than purely military.
records.policy_implication: Military interventions must strictly serve and support a broader political dialogue strategy.

mission_title: Report of the Security Council mission to Yemen, 27 January 2013

main_risks: Obstruction and political spoiling by former regime loyalists and armed elements targeting military restructuring and state infrastructure.
Security fragility driven by Al-Qaida in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP) terrorist attacks, assassinations, and active clashes in northern and southern governorates.
Rising southern separatism and grievances (Al-Hirak) exacerbated by economic exclusion and central governance deficit.
Severe humanitarian crisis with extreme food insecurity, acute child malnutrition, and large IDP/refugee populations.
main_commitments: Government commitment to launch the National Dialogue Conference on 18 March 2013 with guaranteed representation for southerners, women, and youth.
International donor commitment to transform over $7 billion in pledges into concrete economic recovery assistance.
Government willingness to develop and implement a UN action plan to end child recruitment into armed forces.
main_policy_signals: Unwavering Security Council support for President Hadi, the Government of National Unity, and the GCC Initiative political transition.
Explicit warning that the Security Council is ready to consider targeted sanctions under Article 41 of the UN Charter against transition spoilers.
Continued application of sanctions against Al-Qaida in the Arabian Peninsula pursuant to resolution 2083 (2012).
mission_analytics.summary_assessment: The Security Council mission to Yemen on 27 January 2013 aimed to demonstrate strong political support for the ongoing transition process under the GCC Initiative and evaluate compliance with resolution 2051 (2012). The mission noted significant milestones, including peaceful presidential elections, initial military restructuring under a unified command, and preparations for an inclusive National Dialogue Conference. However, it concluded that the transition remains fragile and under direct threat from political spoilers, AQAP terrorism, northern armed clashes, and southern separatist tendencies. The Council reiterated its readiness to impose Article 41 sanctions on spoilers and urged immediate international funding to address Yemen's severe humanitarian and economic crisis.

records.record_text: The primary purpose of the mission was to reaffirm the continued support of the Security Council for the ongoing political transition process in Yemen, in accordance with the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Initiative and Implementation Mechanism leading towards elections in February 2014.
records.political_signal: Unwavering Security Council endorsement of the GCC Initiative and transition roadmap.
records.policy_implication: Reaffirms international backing for President Hadi and the Government of National Unity.

records.record_text: The mission highlighted the Security Council's continued concern about those hindering or interfering in the transition, noting that resolution 2051 (2012) allows for the imposition of sanctions on spoilers.
records.political_signal: Explicit warning to potential political and military spoilers regarding targeted UN sanctions.
records.policy_implication: Establishes deterrence framework against individuals obstructing military restructuring or dialogue.

records.record_text: The mission found that progress has been made in implementing the GCC Initiative and Implementation Mechanism in accordance with resolutions 2014 (2011) and 2051 (2012), noting the successful completion of the first phase with the election of Vice-President Hadi as President.
records.policy_implication: Validates the legal and executive authority of President Hadi.

records.record_text: Achievements in military restructuring, efforts to regain control over territory lost to Al-Qaida in the Arabian Peninsula, and preparations for an all-inclusive National Dialogue Conference have enabled the people of Yemen to step back from the brink of civil war.
records.policy_implication: Demonstrates the effectiveness of joint international-Yemeni mediation.

records.record_text: The Government continues to maintain limited control over parts of its territory, especially in the north and the south, and Al-Qaida and other militant armed groups remain an acute threat.
records.policy_implication: Requires continued security sector reform and counter-terrorism coordination.

records.record_text: Actions aimed at undermining the Government and transition process continue, including politically motivated attacks against oil and gas infrastructure and obstruction of military restructuring and presidential decrees.
records.policy_implication: Underlines the necessity of enforcing resolution 2051 (2012) against recalcitrant regime actors.

records.record_text: The adoption of Yemen's transitional justice law remains pending owing to political deadlock.
records.policy_implication: Impasse hinders national reconciliation and institutional accountability.

records.record_text: In the north, clashes between the Al-Houthi movement, Salafists and tribal groups associated with the Islah Party continue, preventing the Government from re-establishing control, while the Al-Houthis have expanded their presence beyond Sa'ada to Sana'a.
records.policy_implication: Highlights ongoing sub-national armed conflicts complicating state consolidation.

records.record_text: In the south, elements of the Al-Hirak movement calling for independence are increasingly vocal, drawn to extremes in the absence of central government benefits and persistent long-standing grievances since 1990 unification.
records.policy_implication: Addresses southern grievances as a core priority for national dialogue stability.

records.record_text: Military offensives dislodged Al-Qaida elements from Abyan and Shabwa Governorates, but led them to disperse throughout the country and infiltrate major cities, resulting in increased terrorist attacks, sabotage, and assassination attempts against government officials.
records.policy_implication: Demonstrates AQAP's tactical adaptation from territorial control to asymmetric urban terrorism.

records.record_text: The Military Affairs Committee brought armed confrontations between rival military units and militias in Sana'a to an end, removed military units, opened roads, and removed illegal checkpoints.
records.policy_implication: Marks key progress in demilitarizing the capital and restoring public order.

records.record_text: Presidential decrees restructured Yemen's military forces into four major units and integrated independent divisions under seven regional commands and a unified Ministry of Defence authority.
records.policy_implication: Crucial institutional step toward ending command fragmentation in the military.

records.record_text: Children continue to be recruited and used by armed groups and certain elements of the security forces in Yemen.
records.policy_implication: Requires urgent action plan implementation under resolution 1612 (2005).

records.record_text: The Government responded that Yemeni law prohibits recruitment under age 18 and criminalizes offences, stating child soldiers were primarily recruited by other militias and the Ministry of Human Rights was addressing the issue.
records.policy_implication: Reflects official state commitment while highlighting enforcement gaps regarding non-state militias.

records.record_text: UNCT reported that 10 million people lack sufficient access to food, half the population lacks clean water, and over 150,000 severely malnourished children may die without immediate assistance.
records.policy_implication: Demands immediate emergency humanitarian aid scale-up to prevent widespread mortality.

records.record_text: President Hadi called upon the Friends of Yemen to transform over $7 billion in international pledges into concrete assistance.
records.policy_implication: Crucial to stabilize the economy and cushion transition socio-economic pressures.

records.record_text: The Preparatory Committee for the National Dialogue Conference represents all major political constituencies—including GPC, JMP, youth, women, civil society, Houthis, and Al-Hirak—comprising 565 delegates who will make decisions by a 90 per cent consensus.
records.policy_implication: Establishes an unprecedented inclusive governance framework for constitution drafting.

records.record_text: President Hadi established two commissions through Presidential Decree No. 2 on 8 January 2013 to redress long-standing southern grievances concerning land and public employment.
records.policy_implication: Concrete step to build trust and mitigate southern boycott threats against national dialogue.

records.record_text: The Security Council reiterates its call upon all those responsible to abide by paragraph 6 of resolution 2051 (2012) with immediate effect, viewing that further measures, including under Article 41 of the Charter of the United Nations, should be considered against transition spoilers.
records.political_signal: Direct notification that Article 41 sanctions are actively under Council consideration.
records.policy_implication: Prepares legal groundwork for establishing a UN sanctions regime on Yemen.

records.record_text: The Security Council calls upon all donors to provide full funding for the 2013 humanitarian response plan requiring $716 million and urges international partners to transform over $7 billion in pledges into concrete assistance.
records.policy_implication: Essential to prevent economic collapse and support humanitarian delivery.

records.record_text: The Security Council calls upon all Yemeni stakeholders to come together to finalize arrangements that would enable the commencement of the National Dialogue Conference on 18 March 2013 without any further delay.
records.policy_implication: Secures firm launch date for constitutional reform proceedings.
